newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 17.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Finance Minister Ivan Pilip yesterday did as he had promised at the weekend and ignored the law on budget regulations and obtained money for wages for state workers.

- Finance Minister Ivan Pilip expects an increase in prices this year of 10 percent. He said that with budget cuts, wages for state workers will should increase by six percent, which is a real decline in wages of about four percent.
- The IVVM said yesterday that at the beginning of June, the cabinet had the trust of only 22 percent of citizens, 13 percent less than in May and 28 percent less than in January.

- During yesterday's coalition meeting over health reforms, Health Minister Jan Strasky's secretary Miloslav Macek's concept of a health system established on competition between health insurance companies prevailed.

- From the beginning of July, the daily limit for withdrawals from on-line cash dispensers will double. Variant cards, formerly limited at 2,000 crowns daily, will have a limit of 4,000 crowns daily and will be valid for two years from July 1.
- From yesterday, Moravskoslezske Pivovary increased their beer prices by an average of five percent. Plzensky Prazdroj will also increase prices, although it has not announced the extent.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Skodaexport and Moravia Steel won an international tender for the supply of 40,000 tonnes of rails for Turkish state railways. The order is worth $17.058 million, and a contract should be signed in the second half of this month.
- Prumyslovy Penzijni Fond will increase its clients' accounts by 12.1 percent using 10 million crowns from last year's profits of 12.809 million crowns.

- Autopal, which is completely owned by Ford Motor Company, will obtain $50 million in investments from its owner this year and at the beginning of next year for manufacturing lighting systems for Ford Escorts.
- For the first five months of this year, mining company OKD had net profits of about five million crowns. Shareholders predict net profits this year of 35.7 million crowns, identical to last year.

- Karlovarske Mineralni Vody, the largest domestic mineral water maker, had net profits last year of 117 million crowns, a year-on-year increase of 34 million crowns. Revenue increased by one third to 900 million crowns.
- Chepos Brno recently obtained a contract for reconstructing factories in Samara, Russia, for manufacturing fertiliser. The contract is worth $7.3 million.

- The Bureau for Preserving Economic Competition reached a conclusion in the investigation of large store franchises. It found than none of the chains violated laws or misused their dominant position.
- According to the director of Stavby Silnic a Zeleznic a.s., Borivoj Kacena, construction of the first highway financed from the government budget should begin in 1999 at the earliest.

LIDOVE NOVINY - In a general meeting today, shareholders of Poldi Steel should decide on changing into a holding and forming subsidiaries with guaranteed restrictions from current factories. This should help in renewing production.
- Despite being under compulsory administration, there is still interest in Agrobanka's banking services. Deposits of individuals amount to 36 billion crowns.
- The central bank will probably decide today whether it will once again open the market to foreign banks and financial institutions.

- During a tripartite meeting yesterday, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus called on social partners to follow the cabinet's money-saving measures in the private sector. The cabinet approved restructuring of the tripartite council, and all sides are preparing proposals.
- In coming days, members of the foreign committees of German and Austrian parliaments will visit Prague to discuss membership in NATO and the EU.
PRAVO - According to IVVM, 45 percent of citizens were in favour of entry into NATO at the beginning of June, 33 against and 22 uncertain.
- From Monday, Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec has a new deputy, Jan Winkler, formerly the director of the department for analysing and planning at the Foreign Ministry.

- In April, the increase in retail sales was only three percent year-on-year, while they increased in March by 6.4 percent. For the first four months of this year, retail sales increased by 2.1 percent in fixed prices.

- Through its Czech-American joint company ETA, CKD Praha obtained its first contract for manufacturing underground trains and electric components for American streetcars. The contract amounts to only $1.5 million, but it opens the door for other possible contracts in New Orleans.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
